object_context: Fresh analytic child of RH-ANA-002. The active obstruction is to localize the first genuinely sign-sensitive all-index coordinate in an exact zeta-specific arithmetic representation of the Li coefficients. Primary-source retrieval now adds Coffey's exact resummation of the binomial zeta-value term into a convergent series over odd integers with nonnegative summands. This removes that entire term family from the sign bottleneck without assuming RH; the remaining hard coordinate is the eta/Laurent binomial transform together with the explicit affine term.
structural_coordinates: Li's criterion requires lambda_n >= 0 for every positive integer n; finite prefixes are not sufficient.
Bombieri-Lagarias/Coffey give an exact arithmetic representation with an eta/Laurent binomial transform, an explicit affine term, and a binomial zeta-value term.
For S1(n)=sum_{j=2}^n (-1)^j binom(n,j)(1-2^{-j})zeta(j), the identity (1-2^{-j})zeta(j)=sum_{q odd>=1}q^{-j} and finite j-summation yield S1(n)=sum_{q odd>=1}[(1-1/q)^n-1+n/q].
Each odd-integer summand is nonnegative by Bernoulli's inequality for x=1/q in [0,1], and the series converges because its large-q expansion is O_n(q^{-2}).
Therefore coefficientwise absolute-value bounds on the original alternating zeta-value binomial family destroy a known exact cancellation and are methodologically misaligned.
Coffey already records this resummation; the present cycle makes no theorem novelty claim.
The remaining eta coefficients come from the Laurent expansion of -zeta'/zeta at s=1; controlling their binomial transform uniformly in n is the next sign-sensitive arithmetic coordinate.
Brown and Freitas show that finite/modified Li inequalities can encode bounded zero-free regions; partial positivity therefore remains partial zero-location information, not RH.
Lagarias-Voros growth-class routes remain contrastive alternatives, but an unconditional bound strong enough to exclude off-line growth must be audited for root-equivalent strength.
equivalent_formulations: Every nontrivial zero rho of zeta has Re(rho)=1/2.
lambda_n >= 0 for all positive integers n.

In the exact Coffey/Bombieri-Lagarias arithmetic formula, the known nonnegative S1(n) term plus the affine and eta-binomial contributions sum to lambda_n; RH requires the total to remain nonnegative for all n.
solved_analogues: Cancellation-preserving transforms in harmonic/numerical analysis: an alternating expression may become manifestly positive only after exact resummation, while termwise absolute bounds can be exponentially or qualitatively misleading.
Bernoulli remainder identity: (1-x)^n-1+nx is nonnegative on x in [0,1] for integer n>=1.
near_solved_analogues: Coffey's exact odd-integer resummation of the zeta-value/binomial contribution to Li's arithmetic formula.
Brown's and Freitas's Li-type criteria for finite or parameterized zero-free regions, which calibrate what partial Li information can and cannot certify.
Lagarias and Voros asymptotic dichotomies for Li coefficients.

method_transfers.source_context: Coffey's arithmetic decomposition of the Li coefficients
method_transfers.method: Perform exact resummation before applying inequalities, isolate the known-positive zeta-value/binomial component, and move the sign audit to the remaining eta/Laurent coordinate.
required_assumptions: use the exact arithmetic formula and sign convention
justify interchange using finite j-sum and absolutely convergent q-series for j>=2
do not infer anything about the eta-binomial term from positivity of S1(n)
disanalogies: odd integers in S1(n) are not a prime decomposition
positivity of S1(n) does not imply positivity of lambda_n
Coffey's later eta conjectures are not used as premises
method_transfers.repair_question: Can the eta/Laurent binomial transform be reorganized into an exact source-bound representation with a uniform all-n bound that is strictly weaker than RH and preserves cancellation?

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A signed oscillatory representation can look uncontrolled term by term even when an exact transform exposes a stable positive remainder; taking absolute values before the transform destroys the cancellation that carries the useful structure.
source_to_target_mapping: exact transform -> sum over odd q
disanalogies: the target is an exact arithmetic identity, not noisy numerical data
the analogy gives no bound on eta_j and no RH authority
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before bounding a cancellation-heavy arithmetic expression, search for an exact representation in which the preserved cancellation is explicit; bound only the residual that remains sign-sensitive.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Verify the identity algebraically and source-bind it; run hostile checks showing that termwise absolute values lose the known cancellation; do not transfer any sign claim to the eta/Laurent term.
